topicDisplay: The Christian Church through a Study of the Catholic Church and the Protestant Church

promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The nature and features of the Catholic and Protestant traditions
Similarities and differences between the traditions

questions.q: How many sacraments does the Catholic Church recognise?
questions.explain: The Catholic Church recognises seven sacraments: Baptism, Confirmation, Eucharist, Reconciliation, Anointing of the Sick, Holy Orders and Matrimony.

questions.q: Most Protestant churches recognise how many sacraments?
questions.explain: Most Protestants accept only Baptism and the Eucharist (Lord's Supper) as sacraments, since they see these as directly instituted by Jesus.

questions.q: The Catholic belief that the bread and wine become the actual body and blood of Christ is known as:
questions.explain: Transubstantiation is the Catholic teaching that, in the Mass, the substance of the bread and wine truly becomes the body and blood of Christ.

questions.q: Who is regarded as the head of the Catholic Church on earth?
questions.explain: Catholics regard the Pope, the Bishop of Rome, as the successor of St Peter and the visible head of the Church on earth.

questions.q: In which year did Martin Luther's protest spark the Protestant Reformation?
questions.explain: Martin Luther's protest in 1517 is traditionally taken as the beginning of the Protestant Reformation.

questions.q: What is the document Martin Luther is traditionally said to have nailed to the church door in Wittenberg?
questions.explain: The Ninety-Five Theses (1517) attacked abuses such as the sale of indulgences and helped launch the Reformation.

questions.q: The Protestant principle of 'sola scriptura' teaches that:
options: The Bible alone is the supreme authority for faith and practice
The Pope cannot make errors on matters of faith
Church tradition carries equal weight to scripture
Salvation must be earned through good works
questions.explain: 'Sola scriptura' ('scripture alone') means Protestants take the Bible, rather than the Pope or tradition, as the final authority.

questions.q: The Protestant principle of 'justification by faith alone' (sola fide) teaches that salvation comes through:
options: Faith in Jesus Christ rather than good works
questions.explain: Sola fide teaches that people are saved by grace through faith in Christ, not by earning it through works.

questions.q: The Protestant idea of the 'priesthood of all believers' means that:
options: All Christians have direct access to God without a priest as mediator
Only the Pope can forgive sins
Only ordained clergy may read the Bible
Every believer must become an ordained priest
questions.explain: This principle holds that every believer can approach God directly through Christ, without needing a priest to mediate.

questions.q: According to Catholic teaching, authority in the Church comes from:
options: Scripture, Tradition and the Magisterium together
questions.explain: Catholics hold that Scripture, Sacred Tradition and the teaching authority of the Church (Magisterium) work together as sources of authority.

questions.q: The main act of worship in the Catholic Church, centred on the Eucharist, is called the:
questions.explain: The Mass is the central Catholic act of worship, at which the Eucharist is celebrated.

questions.q: In many Protestant services the central feature of worship is:
options: The preaching of the Word (the sermon)
questions.explain: Protestant worship typically focuses on the reading and preaching of the Bible, reflecting the importance of scripture.

questions.q: A visitor enters a church and notices the pulpit, not the altar, is the central focus and the walls are plain with few statues. This is most likely a:
questions.explain: A central pulpit and plain interior reflect the Protestant emphasis on preaching the Word rather than on the altar and imagery.

questions.q: The Catholic belief in a state of purification after death, before a soul enters heaven, is called:
questions.explain: Purgatory is the Catholic teaching that some souls undergo purification after death before entering heaven; Protestants generally reject it.

questions.q: Which practice is characteristic of Catholic worship but generally rejected in Protestant worship?
options: Veneration of Mary and the saints
questions.explain: Catholics honour Mary and the saints and ask their intercession, whereas most Protestants pray directly to God alone.

questions.q: The Catholic sacrament in which a person confesses sins to a priest and receives absolution is:
questions.explain: In Reconciliation the penitent confesses sins to a priest, who grants absolution in God's name.

questions.q: A Baptist congregation baptises only adults who make a personal profession of faith, immersing them fully in water. This practice is known as:
questions.explain: Believers' baptism, practised by Baptists, is given only to those old enough to profess faith personally, usually by full immersion.

questions.q: Which belief is shared by BOTH the Catholic and Protestant traditions?
options: Belief in the Trinity and the resurrection of Jesus
questions.explain: Both traditions are Christian and share core beliefs such as the Trinity and Jesus' death and resurrection, despite their differences.

questions.q: Two Christians discuss Communion. One says the bread truly becomes Christ's body; the other says it is only a symbol recalling Christ's death. Their views represent, respectively:
options: A Catholic and a Protestant understanding
A Protestant and a Catholic understanding
questions.explain: The Catholic view is transubstantiation (real presence), while many Protestants hold a symbolic or memorial understanding of Communion.

questions.q: One key difference between the traditions concerns the clergy: in the Catholic Church priests are normally:
options: Free to marry like other believers
questions.explain: Catholic priests are normally required to be celibate, whereas many Protestant denominations allow their ministers to marry.
